title: Read the Trail Before You Drive
subtitle: Learn to distinguish visible terrain hazards from what you still need to verify.
assetAlt: Illustrated desert trail with a sandstone shelf on the left, scattered rocks in the center, and an eroded rut at the right edge. The distant track curves out of view.
assetStatus: AI-generated instructional illustration; not a photograph of a real route. Obstacles are qualitative and have no measured dimensions.

hazards.name: Sandstone shelf
hazards.explanation: A defined rock lip is visible on the left. Its actual height and the clearance available beneath the vehicle cannot be determined from the image.
hazards.check: Walk the ledge and inspect the front approach, rear departure, and underbody path.

hazards.name: Loose rock field
hazards.explanation: A concentration of displaced rocks is visible. How tightly they are embedded, and whether they will roll under a tire, is unknown.
hazards.check: Inspect tire-sized stones and loose material on foot before choosing tire placement.

hazards.name: Eroded washout
hazards.explanation: A deep-looking eroded channel runs beside the track. A photo cannot establish edge stability or whether the bank can support a tire.
hazards.check: Verify the edge, depth and available vehicle width; do not assume the shoulder is load-bearing.

hazards.name: Unseen exit
hazards.explanation: The track bends out of view. From this viewpoint, you cannot confirm what lies beyond the visible section or where the full vehicle will exit.
hazards.check: Continue scouting until the exit and any subsequent hazards are visible.

evidenceQuestions.prompt: There is a rocky concentration in the middle of the visible track.
evidenceQuestions.explanation: Yes. You can see the rocks; you cannot tell how firmly each is seated.

evidenceQuestions.prompt: The right-hand bank will safely support the full weight of the vehicle.
evidenceQuestions.explanation: Unknown. Surface texture and apparent shape do not reveal the bank's load-bearing capacity.

evidenceQuestions.prompt: The left ledge is lower than the vehicle's approach and breakover clearance.
evidenceQuestions.explanation: Unknown. The image contains no reliable scale or measurements, and the user's vehicle geometry is not supplied.

evidenceQuestions.prompt: The exit of the visible trail is partially hidden by the bend.
evidenceQuestions.explanation: Yes. The sight line ends before the full trail ahead can be evaluated.

decision.prompt: You are stopped in a safe place before the rocky section. What is the most defensible next action?

options.title: Park safely and scout the full obstacle on foot
options.description: Check the shelf, loose rocks, rut edge and exit; verify your vehicle clearance and that the route is open before attempting it.
options.feedback: Best answer. The scene presents multiple unknowns. A deliberate scout produces information needed for a safe plan without extending the trail.

options.title: Drive around the rocks using the right shoulder
options.description: The edge looks smoother than the center.
options.feedback: A smooth-looking edge may be unstable, and leaving the designated route may be prohibited or damage terrain. It also places a tire near the eroded channel.

options.title: Carry momentum through the center
options.description: The suspension and tire size should absorb the rough section.
options.feedback: Vehicle capability does not establish what is beneath the rocks or beyond the blind exit. Momentum can reduce your ability to stop and reassess.

debrief: Confirm the route is legally open and identify the full exit path.
Identify tire paths as well as axle, differential and underbody paths.
Check the stability of edges and loose material rather than guessing from appearance.
Know what would make you stop, use a spotter or turn around.
Stay on the designated trail; never create a bypass by widening the route.

sources.label: Tread Lightly! — Responsible Four Wheeling
sources.note: Stay on designated routes; scout on foot; avoid trail widening.

sources.label: BLM — Off-Highway Vehicles
sources.note: Respect route designations and local restrictions.
